note: The Handover's route scripts (brief 011 B, Waymark), played headless by the mission checker (bun run missions:check handover). Rewritten 2026-10-15 for Keel's round-2 engine: the final fight (N10, N11) and the crowd are on in every script, the cast is M-2's from the promoted people run r016 (sim/data/handover.site.json cast, 2026-10-16; Inez p-cafe-14 Fearful, the guard p-records-office-01, the driver p-records-office-31 and Vale p-records-office-07 Mercenary), so route A helps Inez twice (§04: a Fearful person needs Help ×2), Watch takes 20 s and the fight's shots are untraced (Sky's balance rulings). The scripts start from Keel's scenarios where one exists (N10, N11, N11b, S09, S25, N08), without their fixtures and keeping only the orders the engine took; every fixture a script would need became orders. Keel's readings are kept: the response unit enters from the north street (§07 'west street'), one door guard stays the whole mission, and Vale follows the mission's timeline, not his routine. Closing events (Suture's question; Aster 2026-10-15): route A's is Vale's exit at 5:50 (§07 route A, before 5:50), secured when the Enforcer is inside; route B's is the mission's close, 8:30 since Sky's ruling (rivals take Vale or the car leaves), secured when Vale is with the Enforcer. A carry in progress at the close (Waymark's ruling, 2026-10-15, on Keel's E8): the close ends the take, not a carry already under way. If the Enforcer holds Vale at 8:30 the run goes on (the engine logs horizon.open) and wins only when Vale reaches the getaway car; the final fight, the seal and the Enforcer's health bound the carry. Recommended to Keel and Motive, not yet in the engine: a hard stop at 12:00 (§01: a mission is 8-12 min) where a carry still under way ends as 'district seals'. Brief 013 D (Waymark, 2026-10-16): the takedown engine (Keel 0.5.0, security level 2, the guard's check-in marks every 90 s). Route G takes the guard out (knockout; fast; kill hidden behind the service door). Careless scripts (kind careless) do the same violence seen by a camera, seen by a crowd, found before the exit, or reported unstopped, each against its careful twin (MC-7). Trail is compared in total, the mission's plus what the debrief carries into the campaign. Rev 4 (2026-10-16): a found body holds the doors in its sight (careless-guard-left-door-held); open cases are priced at the rulebook's case-trail-eq in the totals. The driver route (Motive §6.2) is still not scripted: with the pickup loop and three bodies to a service door it plays, but each staff victim's missed mark is its own incident (the second lands at Alert 2, and the search opens the service door), and every witness at the bay tells a Loyal workmate by telephone (briefs/013/waymark-handover.md §5). Brief 018 (Waymark, 2026-10-18; Keel's engine 0.7.0, the getaway): extract is retired into Board and Go. Each quiet route has two references: fight it out (the original id: the Enforcer waits for the crew to break, boards, and the car leaves; the three walk out) and board and go (<id>-board, the primary of A, B and G: the Enforcer walks Vale to the car as the ambush springs, the three board once the blocker is down, nobody left behind). Loud has board and go (loud), fight it out (loud-fight) and the cheapest (loud-fast), each boarding the whole cell, since the seal clock captures anyone left standing. loud-left-downed and loud-left-standing are the two runs that leave an op behind (captured downed; captured fighting, abandoned). Plans may wait for the engine's `blocker.out` (c019: the engine logs it, and `car.free`). c019 (engine 0.7.x: walking Vale, the Enforcer does not fire): plans recomposed; loud-fast keeps its cover and carries its downed Fixer in. MC-10 checks quiet beats loud on Trail (a captive's +4 T counts as campaign Trail), Alert, Standing and the seal; MC-11 that no ambush spot or police stand holds the car. Brief 031 (Waymark, 2026-10-20; Keel's engine 0.11.0: every agent Watches at its own reach, and security watchers notice loiterers: a clock per watcher and agent, running while the agent stands still in its sight, noticed at 8 s, wary at 20 s, reported at 45 s at the Handover's Heat 0, mission.json start.heat): every quiet and loud route's waits are re-sited out of sight, so no watcher that keeps a clock sees an agent stand. The Enforcer waits on the forecourt (56.5, -47.5), behind the entrance camera's cone and the patrol's sweep and outside the guard's, and goes to the door's south side only once the patrol has left (A, loud) or walks in for the blow (G); in route B the Scout watches the driver from the Office's south-west corner and waits for the tip 2.8 m outside the pickup camera's cone, and the Fixer walks to the driver as the Watch ends; in route G the Scout watches the guard from 27.4 m, beyond his cone. A Watch in reach starts where the agent stands, so a Watch step waits (gap) for the walk to its spot. Every script states the Alert it ends at (expects.alert); MC-12 checks that no quiet script is reported for loitering and that the careless-loiter twin costs more than its careful twin. The fail scripts keep their fail codes; where a careless player's agent stands in a camera's view, it is now reported (Alert 1), which they keep.

Nobody sees the car leave, so it costs 1 T less than loud and 2.2 s more. c022 (brief 023): holstered until the fight as loud, and without the close on the café wall (walking out at the officers got the Scout and the Tech downed): the cell downs both officers from the cover by the car; 4:42.2, 9 T. Engine 0.14 (tuning.md §7.9-§7.11: the kite response, the 16 m sidearm, police in cover returning fire out to 16 m): fighting it out with the police no longer saves the whole cell; the Tech is downed going for the car and captured (+4 T).
